evidence.source_assertion: Methods state that WT and mutant FucO preparations for site-directed-mutagenesis studies used pGEX3X/pCM2 in BL21(DE3), with GST removed by factor Xa to avoid the His6 tag.

Results compare D196L, H200A and H200F metal contents with WT examined in parallel, reporting 0.53 Fe atom/subunit for WT. Read with the preparation Methods, this supports the cleaved-WT comparator attribution, not His6 crystal occupancy.

after.text: The 2005 source reports earlier Cu(II)/Cd(II) FucO inhibition and cites PMID4306747. Retained evidence for the older paper is abstract/landing material; its full experimental body was not inspected. Figure 4 tests Zn/Fe, so no Cu/Cd dose, EG oxidation effect, binding mechanism or new causal edge is asserted.

evidence.source_assertion: The 2005 discussion reports earlier FucO inhibition by Cu(II) and Cd(II), citing reference 40. This is prior-work context; the adjacent Figure 4 experiment addresses Zn/Fe.
Reference 40 links the earlier oxidoreductase study to PMID4306747. This citation identifies the prior report; it does not supply a freshly inspected older experimental body.

description-source-crosswalk.json.before: Current FucO P0A9S1 is 382 residues, whereas the 2005/2023 papers use historical 383-residue numbering and older P11549 context. Their Asp196/His200/His263/His277 Fe ligands, G17D/G97E/D39G, N-terminal deletion and I7L/L8V engineering labels are not silently renumbered onto the current reference. The structure has one Fe site per chain but solution WT Fe occupancy was about 0.53. His267 is not the Fe ligand formerly proposed. N-terminal strand exchange supports the dimer; historical deltaN10 loses assembly/activity. The pQE32/pCM1 His6 preparation in M15(pREP4) differs from pGEX3X/pCM2 in BL21 and its cleaved WT/mutant preparations. Two NAD sites per dimer and D39G cofactor expansion do not create a wild-type NADPH core. Older partially purified mutant enzyme also used added manganese; that preparation-specific alternative is retained.
description-source-crosswalk.json.after: Current FucO P0A9S1 is 382 residues, whereas the 2005/2023 papers use historical 383-residue numbering and older P11549 context. Their Asp196/His200/His263/His277 Fe ligands, G17D/G97E/D39G, N-terminal deletion and I7L/L8V engineering labels are not silently renumbered onto the current reference. The pQE32/pCM1 N-terminal His6 preparation in M15(pREP4) supports the one-Fe-site crystal observation. Separately, solution metal analysis compared D196L/H200A/H200F mutants with WT containing 0.53 Fe atom/subunit. Methods assign WT/mutant site-directed-mutagenesis preparations to pGEX3X/pCM2 in BL21(DE3), with GST removed by factor Xa; this Methods/Results join supports the cleaved-WT comparator attribution, not a measured occupancy for the His6 crystal preparation. His267 is not the Fe ligand formerly proposed. N-terminal strand exchange supports the dimer; historical deltaN10 loses assembly/activity. Two NAD sites per dimer and D39G cofactor expansion do not create a wild-type NADPH core. Older partially purified mutant enzyme also used added manganese; that preparation-specific alternative is retained. The 2005 paper reports earlier Cu(II)/Cd(II) inhibition of FucO, citing PMID4306747. Its retained older-source evidence is abstract/landing material, not an inspected full experimental body; no Cu/Cd dose or direct assay is inferred. The 2005 Figure 4 experiment separately tests Zn/Fe.
